newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian dollar ends flat in active trading.
newsitem.headline: Canadian dollar ends flat in active trading.

text.p: * The Canadian dollar ended relatively flat at C$1.3397 (US$0.7464) from Wednesday's close at C$1.3400 (US$0.7462). * The unit weakened from this morning's open of C$1.3385 in concert with a softer U.S. dollar, traders said * Canadian dollar expected to benefit from long-term bullish sentiment * Little impact on unit from Canada retail sales data
The Canadian dollar has undergone a correction recently, weakening to around C$1.3440 (US$0.7440) from year-long highs near C$1.3291 (US$0.7523) within the last month.
"Just the business that we saw today indicates that there is strong interest to buy the Canadian dollar again," the trader said.
In other news, traders said Canadian retail sales for September had little impact on the currency.
Statistics Canada reported on Thursday that retail sales rose 0.2 percent to C$17.93 billion from a revised C$17.89 billion in August.
The September sales figures were lower than economists' forecasts of a 0.4 percent rise, but Statistics Canada said in its report that early indications of October retail sales point to an increase
On the crosses, the Canada unit rose to 1.1175 marks from Wednesday's close of 1.1164 marks, but eased to 83.03 yen from 83.21 yen.
